findings: The one new constant-variance arm is a direct control for the input-dependent variance pathway: applying the existing logvariance head to hidden*0 makes its output depend only on two biases while retaining the R7 parameter topology and initialization.

The design correctly states the optimization confound: constant variance removes variance-to-trunk gradients after the R7 heteroskedastic weights can become nonzero, so the comparison cannot isolate variance expressivity from optimization coupling or establish latent-noise recovery.
Primary and secondary contrast directions are explicit; both compare one new endpoint against compact stored R7 scores, with no R7 rerun, evaluation-driven selection, CV, or tuning.
The adaptive exposed-panel boundary, fixed seed/recipe/masks, one-endpoint rule, fit-only normalization, finite training counters, and bounded CPU-only resource envelope are stated.
limitations_preserved: One seed and an adaptively exposed panel do not provide a training-variation interval or fresh/full-fold estimate.
A constant-arm match would weaken the input-dependent-variance explanation for this pilot; an advantage would motivate confirmation, not prove noise recovery.
The finite objective comparison does not establish public, CP30, or full-model performance.
review_scope: Bounded pre-code scientific design review only; no implementation, panel arrays, model/checkpoint loads, or execution.
